transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
China is denying allegations that it carried out a spy operation targeting the CEO of computer
chip giant Nvidia Jensen Huang.
NPR's Jennifer Pack has more from Beijing.
American officials have been blocking China's access to its most advanced chipsets, yet
Huang has criticized this policy.
President Trump eventually let Nvidia sell chips to China, just less advanced ones.
Now Huang admits having an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence alleged is a Chinese spy.
China's foreign ministry calls the so-called Chinese spy narrative an attempt to smear
China.
Chinese media have downplayed the spy aspect of the story.
On Michael blogging platform Weibo, the hashtag Jensen Huang admits to cheating has racked
up over 580 million views.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Shares of Nvidia are lower this morning, though Wall Street futures are mostly higher.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio is in Paris for meetings with G7 foreign ministers.
As Rebecca Rossman reports, Iran and Ukraine are expected to be major topics of discussion.
The latest two-day meeting of allies kicks off today in Paris.
The talks begin as Rubio's G7 counterparts face uncertainty about how last week's midterm
defeat might affect the Trump administration's foreign policy approach.
Major topics on the agenda include the Iran conflict and ending the war in Ukraine.
The meeting coincides with separate U.S.-mediated peace talks between Moscow and Kyiv in Abu
Dhabi.
The French foreign minister says Europe will be a part of those talks, but it wasn't immediately
clear how the bloc would be represented.
And governments have said they're concerned the U.S. might be pushing Ukraine for a deal
that would favor Russia.
Rebecca Rossman and Pierre News, Paris.
U.N. climate talks are getting underway today in Turkey.
The COP 31 summit, as it's known, follows this year's deadly heatwaves in Europe and
devastating floods in Nepal fueled by rising global temperatures.
Reservoirs in the southwestern U.S. have gotten a boost from recent rounds of heavy rains.
NPR's Rebecca Herscher reports.
Many reservoirs in the southwest were running dangerously low over the summer because of
a multi-year mega-drought in the region.
Such droughts are more likely because of climate change.
The reservoirs provide water for drinking, irrigation, and industry.
The most famous is Lake Powell, which is the second largest reservoir in the U.S.
It reached record low levels in September.
But rainstorms in October and November brought much-needed water to the region, even as the
storms caused major flood damage in some places.
The water level in Lake Powell is now 20 feet higher than it was in late September, although
it is still far from being full.
Rebecca Herscher, NPR News.
This is NPR News from Washington.
President Trump tells CBS's 60 Minutes he believes the war with Iran and high fuel prices
were among the main reasons why Democratic candidates registered sweeping winds in last
week's midterm elections.
But the president says the primary reason for the GOP losses in his view was that his
name was not on the ballot.
The president added his administration's crackdown on illegal immigration and deportation
policies were too tough at times.
NASA is looking for astronauts, NPR's Chantalice Duster reports.
For the first time in more than two years, NASA is accepting applications from those
interested in becoming an astronaut.
NASA Administrator Jarek Isaacman says those chosen could live and work on the moon.
U.S. citizens can apply, and there are requirements, such as a master's degree in a STEM-related
field.
A NASA spokesperson told NPR the number of astronaut candidates selected will depend
on "mission needs and projected spaceflight rates."
There are currently 32 active NASA astronauts.
The process is competitive.
Out of more than 8,000 applicants for NASA's last astronaut class, only 10 candidates were
selected.
The agency is accepting applications through Dec. 3.
Chantalice Duster, NPR News.
Georgia is once again number one in the Associated Press' top 25 college football rankings.
Utah moves to number two this week, and Notre Dame is in the third spot following its 31-24
win over previously unbeaten and top-ranked Miami.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: China denies spying on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after Huang admits affair with alleged Chinese spy
Nvidia shares lower this morning as Wall Street futures are mostly higher
Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets G7 foreign ministers in Paris on Iran and Ukraine
UN climate talks COP 31 open in Turkey after deadly heatwaves and Nepal floods
Southwestern U.S. reservoirs, including Lake Powell, rise after October and November rains
Trump tells 60 Minutes Iran war and fuel prices contributed to Democratic midterm gains
